THIS MFA COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
 JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI V.HOSMANI  -2-  NC: 2026:KHC-D:3440  MFA No. 102302 of 2018  HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri Siddappa Sajjan, learned counsel for appellant and Sri SC Bhuti, learned counsel for respondent.
2.
Challenging judgment and award dated 30.01.2018 passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, and M.A.C.T. No.V, Jamkhandi1, this appeal is filed.
3. Learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted on 20.05.2016, when claimant along with her relatives was travelling in NWKRTC Bus no.KA-29/F- 1081 from Jamakhandi towards Savalagi, near Hirepadasalagi, driver drove it in a rash and negligent manner and bus dashed against electric poll and caused accident.
In said accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries and despite taking treatment at Dr. G.N. Sanadi Hospital, Jamakhandi, she did not recover fully and suffered loss of earning capacity.
For short, 'Tribunal' NC: 2026:KHC-D:3440 HC-KAR 4. Claiming compensation for same, she filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, against NWKRTC.
5. On appearance, claim petition was opposed on all counts.
Based on contentions, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant examined herself as PW1 and Dr. G.N. Sanadi as PW2 and got marked documents at Exs.P1 to P13.
Respondent did not lead any evidence.

sentences.text:
On consideration, Tribunal held accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus driver and claimant was entitled for compensation assessed as follows:
Pain & Suffering including 25,000/- attendance charges Towards Medical Expenses 65,082/-
 Loss of future income 1,26,000/-
 Towards other expenses 10,000/-
 Total Rs.2,26,000/-

7. Dissatisfied with quantum of compensation,
claimant was in appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3440 HC-KAR  8.

It was firstly submitted, though claimant sustained grievous injuries namely i) Grade 2 compound fracture radius left side and ii) Circumferential Cut lacerated wound over cubital fossa of left elbow joint with injury to elbow joint muscles and nerves, PW2-doctor assessed 42% disability to left upper limb and issued Ex.P12-disability certificate, Tribunal considered loss of earning capacity at only 10%, which was inadequate and sought for enhancement.
9.

It was submitted Tribunal awarded inadequate compensation towards pain and suffering and other incidental expenses and Tribunal erred in not awarding any compensation towards loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period.

10. It was further submitted that as on date of accident i.e., 20.05.2016, claimant was aged 45 years working as coolie and earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3440 HC-KAR Tribunal erred in considering income at Rs.7,500/- per month.
On said grounds sought for allowing appeal.

11. On other hand, learned counsel for respondent- NWKRTC opposed appeal and submitted that Tribunal had already determined compensation under all eligible heads and there was no scope for enhancement.
It was submitted that interest at rate of 9% was excessive and offset any scope of enhancement and sought for dismissal of appeal.

sentences.text: 12. Heard learned counsel for parties and perused impugned judgment, award and record.
13. In this appeal, claimant is seeking for enhancement of compensation.

Therefore, only point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed for?
14.

Though claimant stated that she was aged 45 years working as coolie and earning Rs.12,000/-
per month, same was not substantiated.
In absence, notional income NC: 2026:KHC-D:3440 HC-KAR for year 2016 was considered.
But notional income for said period was Rs.8,750/- per month.
Tribunal was not justified in taking it at Rs.7,500/- per month.
15. Further, wound certificate and treatment records would indicate that claimant has sustained Grade 2 compound fracture of radius left side.
PW2 assessed disability at 42% to left upper limb.
However, PW2 has not stated about loss of earning capacity.

16. Perusal of Ex.P12-disability certificate as well as deposition of PW2 would indicate that there was restriction of movement at left shoulder joint, elbow joint and wrist joint, left hand and fingers,
which would affect employment and earning of claimant as a coolie to some extent.

Therefore,
assessment of loss of earning capacity at 10% by Tribunal would appear inadequate.
Hence, it is appropriate to enhance it to 15%.

17. Thus compensation towards future loss of income would be Rs.8,750 X 15% X 12 X 14 =
Rs.2,20,500/-
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3440 HC-KAR 18.
Tribunal has awarded Rs.65,082/- towards medical expenses, same is confirmed.

However,
considering injury and inpatient treatment for 10 days, compensation awarded towards pain and suffering at Rs.25,000/- apart from Rs.10,000/- attendant charges, are found justified.
19. Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of income during laid up period.

Since,
claimant sustained fracture.
Normally same requires at least three months to heal.
Taking said period as layoff, claimant is awarded Rs.26,250/- towards same.

20. Considering age, occupation and disability sustained, claimant is awarded to Rs.30,000/-
towards loss of amenities.

21. Thus, total compensation would be;
 Pain and suffering 25,000/-
 Towards Medical Expenses 65,082/-
 Loss of income during laid up period 26,250/-

Towards attendant charges 10,000/-
 Towards future loss of income 2,20,500/-

sentences.text:
. Accordingly, point framed for consideration is answered as partly in affirmative as discussed above and this Court pass following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii. Appellant is held entitled to receive Rs.3,76,832/- as against Rs.2,26,00/- awarded by Tribunal with interest of 9% p.a., from date of petition till deposit.
iii. Respondent is directed to deposit enhanced compensation before Tribunal within a period of eight (8) weeks from date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
iv. On deposit, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is ordered to be released and remaining amount is ordered to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any nationalized Bank for a period of five years.
